note: A style flavours wording the coach would vouch for. It never licenses an invented idiom.

default.name: educated native, spoken
default.voice: how a well-read colleague actually talks: contractions, short clauses, no bookish words used for effect

default.name: storyteller
default.voice: one small concrete scene, past tense, the point landing in the last sentence

Food.name: Mark Wiens
Food.voice: food vlogger: present tense, mid-bite reactions, sensory verbs, honest superlatives - 'the flavour is unbelievable', 'you get that smokiness right at the back'

Inspiration.name: TED closing line
Inspiration.voice: one idea, stated plainly, then turned outward to the listener; short sentence last

Inspiration.name: Obama cadence
Inspiration.voice: measured, pauses that carry weight, triples and repeated openings, 'not because it is easy, but because'

Inspiration.name: Brene Brown
Inspiration.voice: research language made personal: names the feeling, owns the discomfort, no polish over the hard part

Computer.name: Steve Jobs keynote
Computer.voice: short declaratives, one number that matters, a pause before the point - 'and it just works'

Computer.name: explain-it-to-the-team
Computer.voice: one analogy from ordinary life, then the mechanism in plain words, no jargon left undefined

Sports.name: play-by-play
Sports.voice: present tense, rising energy, verbs first, the name of the player before the action

Sports.name: post-match interview
Sports.voice: modest, first person plural, credit outward, cliches used the way players really use them

Joke.name: stand-up beat
Joke.voice: set-up in one breath, misdirection, punchline as the last three words - never explained afterwards

Joke.name: dry British understatement
Joke.voice: the disaster described as a mild inconvenience, delivered flat

Joke.name: self-deprecating office humour
Joke.voice: the speaker is the butt of it, small workplace detail, said in passing rather than performed

Empathy.name: reflective listening
Empathy.voice: names back what was heard before adding anything, no advice unless asked, unhurried

Empathy.name: close friend
Empathy.voice: plain and warm, no therapy vocabulary, offers something specific rather than 'let me know if you need anything'

Empathy.name: condolence register
Empathy.voice: formal but not stiff, short sentences, says the thing directly instead of around it

Greeting.name: warm host
Greeting.voice: uses the name, one specific question rather than 'how are you', makes room for the other person to answer

Greeting.name: casual local
Greeting.voice: reduced forms and idiom the way people greet each other in the street, not the phrasebook version
